I found one semantic issue: sample code prints Redis access keys to the console, which can expose secrets in logs. No prompt injection or malicious exfiltration intent was found in SKILL.md.

remediation.issue: Redis access keys are printed in sample code.
remediation.suggestion: Remove Console.WriteLine output for keys and show safe storage through a secret manager.

remediation.issue: A blob export example uses a SAS token-like placeholder in a URL.
remediation.suggestion: Show storage URLs and SAS tokens loaded from secure configuration instead of inline literals.

remediation.issue: Service principal secret variables appear in setup instructions.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer managed identity or workload identity, and warn users not to commit secret values.

content.user_title: Manage Azure Redis with .NET ARM SDK
content.value_statement: Azure Redis management requires many ARM SDK calls and security choices. This skill gives focused .NET patterns for provisioning, updating, securing, and connecting Redis caches.
actual_capabilities: Shows package setup for Azure.ResourceManager.Redis and Azure.Identity.
Explains DefaultAzureCredential and subscription resource access.
Provides create, read, update, delete, and reboot workflows for Redis caches.
Covers firewall rules, patch schedules, access keys, and key regeneration.
Describes import, export, SKU limits, and StackExchange.Redis handoff.
Lists common pitfalls for Premium features and long provisioning times.
limitations: It covers management-plane operations, not Redis data-plane reads, writes, or pub/sub.
Examples must be adapted with real subscription, resource group, and cache names.
Premium-only features require the correct Azure Cache for Redis SKU.
It does not validate current Azure SDK versions or live service availability.

use_cases.title: Provision production caches
use_cases.description: Create or update Azure Cache for Redis instances with SKU, TLS, tags, and long-running operation patterns.

use_cases.title: Secure Redis access
use_cases.description: Review firewall rules, TLS settings, key rotation, and private endpoint management for Redis deployments.

use_cases.title: Plan data migration
use_cases.description: Use import, export, and StackExchange.Redis connection examples after ARM resources are ready.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Redis cache
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to show the Azure.ResourceManager.Redis steps for creating a Standard Azure Cache for Redis in .NET.

prompt_templates.title: Read and update a cache
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to explain how to get an existing Redis cache and update memory policy or SKU in .NET.

prompt_templates.title: Secure access settings
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to design firewall rules, TLS settings, key rotation, and private endpoint checks for an Azure Redis cache.

prompt_templates.title: Build migration workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to plan a Premium SKU import and export workflow, including long-running operations and data-plane connection steps.

output_examples.input: User asks how to create an Azure Redis cache with the .NET management SDK.
output_examples.output: A step sequence covering packages, DefaultAzureCredential, resource group lookup, cache configuration, and create-or-update operation.

output_examples.input: User asks how to rotate Redis access keys safely.
output: Use the management SDK key regeneration operation.
Do not print keys in logs.
Update dependent applications through a secret manager.

output_examples.input: User asks whether Premium Redis features are available.
output_examples.output: A SKU-aware answer that separates Basic, Standard, and Premium capabilities before suggesting patch schedules or import/export.

best_practices: Use DefaultAzureCredential with managed identity or workload identity when possible.
Set TLS 1.2 minimum and keep the non-SSL port disabled.
Store Redis keys and SAS tokens in a secret manager, not logs or source files.
anti_patterns: Do not use this skill for Redis data-plane commands such as get, set, or pub/sub.
Do not print Redis access keys, connection strings, or SAS tokens.
Do not assume Premium-only features work on Basic or Standard caches.

faq.question: Is this for Redis data operations?
faq.answer: No. It covers Azure management operations. Use StackExchange.Redis for data operations.

faq.question: Which package does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers Azure.ResourceManager.Redis and related Azure.Identity authentication patterns for .NET.

faq.question: Can it create and delete caches?
faq.answer: Yes. It shows management-plane create, update, get, delete, and long-running operation patterns.

faq.question: Does it cover firewall rules?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes Redis firewall rule creation, listing, and deletion examples.

faq.question: Does it require Azure credentials?
faq.answer: Yes. Azure ARM operations require credentials with permissions for the target subscription and resource group.

faq.question: Can it manage Premium features?
faq.answer: Yes. It describes patch schedules, import/export, and geo-replication constraints for Premium SKU.
